**Published online:**
September 2, 2026 (Reuters)

**Geographic focus:**
Global — with primary focus on USA, Europe (UK, France, Germany), New Zealand, and Middle East (Iran conflict as trigger)

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
A Reuters market briefing from September 2, 2026, covering a global risk-off environment driven by Iran war-related energy price surges. US 10-year Treasury yields have hit highs not seen since 2023 at 4.8%, approaching the psychologically critical 5% level. Rate hikes are now widely expected from the Fed, ECB, and BoJ this month. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and board member Michael Barr have both signaled September hike support. New Zealand's RBNZ already moved with a second consecutive hike. Political pressures from European budgets, German state elections, and US midterms add complexity. AI earnings (Dell, Palo Alto, Broadcom) provide a marginal counterweight. Labor market data is a secondary driver for the Fed, with above-target inflation the primary concern.

---

Relevance: YES — The article directly addresses US 10-year Treasury yields (4.8%, eyeing 5%), explicit Fed rate hike signals from Chair Warsh and board member Barr, equity market pressure, and upcoming US labor market data.

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: **+80** — Strongly hawkish. Both the Fed Chair (Warsh) and a centrist board member (Barr) have explicitly backed a September hike. Energy-driven inflation, rising yields, and a rate-hiking posture at peer central banks (RBNZ, ECB, BoJ) all reinforce the hawkish tilt. There is no dovish signal or pushback present in the article.
